title: Billing and pricing basics – Coda
text:
# Coda’s billing model 

With Coda’s unique Maker billing model, we only charge for Doc Makers in paid workspaces. Editors and viewers are entirely free!

ℹ️ A quick note on role definitions:

- Doc Makers are workspace members who have the ability to create docs, create pages, and use Coda AI
- Editors have the ability to update existing pages, but can’t create new docs or pages.

To learn more about the different roles and their abilities, check out this comprehensive article.

 When you upgrade to a paid plan, you have the choice of paying annually or monthly. You can use your self-service billing account to change payment methods, update billing details, change pricing plans, and. For more info on managing your billing account, check out this article.

# Available pricing plans 

Coda offers a range of pricing plans, so there’s sure to be one that fits the needs of you and your team.

- Free - Choose this plan if you're just getting started on Coda. You'll be able to share docs with as many people as you like, and even keep your docs organized with folders. Personal docs won’t have any size or object limits. And if you outgrow the Free plan, you can easily upgrade down the line.
- Pro - This plan is ideal if you plan on building large docs, but won't be working actively with a team. You'll have no cap on the doc size and access to more automations and Packs.
- Team - The key is in the name - if you're planning on collaborating with a team, select this option. You'll get more automations and Packs, and doc protection features for added control.
- Enterprise - Choose this plan if you're planning on rolling out Coda across multiple teams or departments. With increased scalability (through SSO), hands-on support, and additional admin controls, this plan allows you to get the most out of Coda. We'll help you find the custom fit for your situation.

For detailed, up-to-date information on our pricing plans - and what’s included in each plan - check out our pricing page.

...

Do I also pay for workspace admins?

Yes - workspace admins are a type of Doc Maker. Therefore, you pay for each workspace admin and Doc Maker in your workspace.

How much does each pricing plan cost?

With our Maker billing model, you only pay for Doc Makers in your workspace. Each pricing plan (Free, Pro, Team, and Enterprise) has a different cost per Doc Maker. To see the cost per Doc Maker, head to our pricing page.

What roles do I pay for and why?

To upgrade a free workspace to a paid one, you only need to pay for a single Doc Maker to get started. As you grow into your workspace, you can invite additional members to become Doc Makers in your workspace. At the end of each billing cycle, you will be billed for the workspace based on how many Doc Makers there are. Any changes to the number of Doc Makers in the workspace mid-cycle are automatically prorated.

When will I get billed for my workspaces?

For our Pro and Team tiers: When you sign up for a new plan, you will be billed up front for all the Doc Makers in your workspace. If you add a new paid user to your workspace (or upgrade an existing one), we'll prorate them for the remainder of your billing cycle. On the annual plan, you will be charged monthly for these additional membership changes, with prorations applied for the remainder of the billing year.

title: Coda Review 2026: Superhuman Docs Pricing and Verdict
text:
TL;DR

Yes, Coda is worth it in 2026 for teams where a few people build docs and many people fill them in, because only Doc Makers pay. Coda is now sold as Superhuman Docs: Pro costs $12 per Doc Maker a month billed annually ($15 monthly), Business costs $33 ($40 monthly), and Editors and Viewers are free.

That pricing rule is the whole story. A 20-person team with 3 Doc Makers pays $432 a year on annual Pro, while Notion Plus bills every member and comes to $2,400 for the same team. If everyone on the team builds, the advantage shrinks, and Business is pricier per head than Notion or ClickUp.

Roles decide the bill. A Doc Maker can create docs, templates and folders, add pages and configure locking. An Editor can edit existing docs and still add tables, views, formulas, buttons and automations. Superhuman's FAQ says Editors and Viewers are always free and the workspace is billed for its Doc Makers, prorated when the count changes mid-cycle.

That means an Editor can do most day-to-day work without a seat. The limit is creation: anyone who needs to start new docs from scratch or manage folders must be a Doc Maker, so a team where everyone spins up their own docs pays for everyone.

The free plan is a real trial, not a permanent home for a team. It limits pages and objects in shared docs, caps attachments at 1 GB per doc, keeps 7 days of version history and gives a low automation quota with manual connector refresh. Pro lifts doc size limits, raises attachments to 5 GB per doc, keeps 30 days of history and refreshes connectors daily. Business makes automations, history and attachments unlimited and refreshes connectors hourly, which matters once docs pull live data from other tools every day.

## Coda (Superhuman Docs) pricing

How much does Coda cost? Free costs nothing. Pro is billed per Doc Maker, and so is Business, each with a discount for annual billing over monthly. Enterprise is quote-only through sales and adds SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, audit events and HIPAA compliance on request.

Techpresso data: what a 20-person team pays. We priced one team of 20 with 3 people who build docs and 17 who only edit them, on annual billing everywhere. Coda bills the 3 makers: $432 a year on Pro and $1,188 on Business. Smartsheet also leaves contributors free, so its Pro plan bills 3 members for $324 a year and Business $684. Notion bills every member: $2,400 a year on Plus and $4,800 on Business. ClickUp upgrades the whole workspace, so Core costs $2,160 a year and Business $4,080.

title: Coda Pricing 2026: Real Costs and How to Choose Your ...
text:
## Coda pricing plans: at a glance

Here's how Coda's four plans compare in terms of pricing and key features. Full plan details and the latest feature breakdowns live on Coda's pricing page.

| Plan | Price | Best for | Key features |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | Individuals and small teams testing Coda | Unlimited Doc Makers, free Packs, AI to try, doc size limits |
| Pro | $12/month per Doc Maker | Power users needing larger docs and branding | Unlimited doc size, hidden pages, custom branding, 30-day version history |
| Team | $36/month per Doc Maker | Growing teams with cross-doc workflows | Unlimited automations, unlimited version history, doc locking, AI included |
| Enterprise | Custom | Larger organizations with security needs | SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs, advanced controls |

Annual billing knocks the Pro plan down to $10/month per Doc Maker and the Team plans down to $30/month per Doc Maker, a ~17% discount.

## How Coda’s Doc Maker pricing works

Before going through each plan, the Doc Maker model needs a quick explanation, because it changes how you should think about cost.

Coda charges only for Doc Makers, the people who create or own documents. Editors and viewers are free across every plan. If your team has 50 people who read and comment on docs but only 4 people who build them, you pay for 4 Doc Makers, not 50. If that model does not suit your team, compare these Coda alternatives.

The catch: if you need every team member to build their own docs, the cost scales up fast. A 20-person team where everyone creates docs costs $200/month on Pro (annual billing) or $720/month on Team (monthly billing).

...

### Pro: $12/month per Doc Maker (or $10/month with annual billing)

What’s included: Everything in Free, plus unlimited doc size, hidden pages, custom branding, 30-day version history, and access to Pro Packs (a broader integration library).

Best for: Solo founders, freelancers, and small teams that need larger docs and a more branded experience without team-level admin features.

- Removes the doc size limit: That's the biggest friction point on Free.
- Custom branding and hidden pages: Make Pro usable for client-facing work.
- Per-Doc-Maker pricing: Small teams stay affordable as they add viewers.

- 30-day version history: Short if you need to look further back.
- No unlimited automations: Workflow-heavy use cases will hit limits.
- No cross-doc syncing: Multi-doc setups feel disconnected.

Notion is generally better for most solo founders because it's easier to learn, has a strong free plan, and costs $10/user/month at the Plus tier. Coda is still active but was rebranded to Superhuman Docs on July 8, 2026 after being acquired by Superhuman, the company behind Grammarly and Superhuman Mail. Existing docs, pricing, and features carried over unchanged, and the product is still commonly referred to as Coda.

title: Coda Review — $0/mo for Solo Founders [4.1/5] | SaaSLens
text:
We rate Coda 4.1/5. More powerful formulas than Notion, making it especially useful for solopreneurs and startups. The main tradeoff: steeper learning curve. The free tier softens this considerably.

## About Coda

Coda is a doc-powered workspace that combines documents, spreadsheets, and applications into one flexible surface. Think of it as Notion meets Google Sheets with more powerful automation.

The free Doc Maker plan includes unlimited docs with 50 objects (tables, views, pages) and 1,000 rows per doc. Pro ($12/maker/month) adds unlimited objects and rows, automations, and cross-doc features. Team ($36/maker/month) adds admin controls and locked templates.

Coda's tables are more powerful than Airtable's — formulas reference other tables, buttons trigger actions, and controls (sliders, dropdowns, date pickers) make interactive interfaces. Packs connect to 600+ services, pulling in data from Slack, Gmail, Jira, and more.

For solo founders, Coda excels at building custom workflows: project trackers, OKR systems, product specs, and team rituals. The doc-first approach feels more natural than Airtable's database-first model.

Limitations: steep learning curve for advanced formulas, the free tier's row limit is restrictive, and the platform can feel overwhelming. For simpler needs, Notion is more approachable.

title: Notion vs Obsidian vs Coda for Solo Founders (2026) - The Real AI Operator
text:
I haven’t built anything production-grade in Coda myself, so the framing below comes from Coda’s docs, a few hours in a friend’s workspace, and threads on their subreddit. If you want hands-on impressions, the template gallery is the fastest way to see what it can do.

Coda looks like a document tool. Underneath it is a builder platform. Pages hold regular text, but they also run tables that behave like databases, buttons that trigger automations, and packs that connect to Google Calendar, Slack, Stripe, and roughly 700 other services. A single Coda doc can replace the spreadsheet you’ve been emailing around, the CRM you built in Airtable, and the half-finished internal tool your contractor keeps scoping and never quite finishes.

Coda’s pricing model is the most generous of the three for small teams. Only “Doc Makers” pay. Viewers and editors are free. If you have a doc your whole team reads but only you update, they don’t add to your bill. The free plan is unlimited for viewers and capped at a small number of Doc Makers.

...

## Pricing for a one-person company

What you pay boils down to two things: how many people touch the workspace and which features you actually use. Here’s what a solo founder sees in August 2026.

- Notion: Free for personal use. Plus runs $10 per member per month on annual billing ($12 if you go monthly). Most solo folks stay on Free until they hit the file upload cap or need longer page history.
- Obsidian: The desktop app is free on every platform. If you want your iPad and phone to stay in sync, add Obsidian Sync at $4 a month, billed annually.
- Coda: Free for unlimited viewers. Pro is $10 per Doc Maker per month on annual billing. Most solo founders stick with Free because there’s only one of you editing.

The catch nobody mentions upfront: Notion bills per member, including people who just read. Coda bills per Doc Maker. So if you share your workspace with five advisors who only read, Notion charges you for six seats. Coda charges you for one. I set up a Notion workspace for a client a while back and handed out a few guest logins without thinking too hard about it. The bill at the end of the month made me wince.

Flip the math to a 20-person team and it reverses. Notion’s flat per-seat pricing usually beats Coda’s free-viewer play once everyone’s actively editing. So don’t pick on pricing alone. Look at who’s actually writing in the doc versus who’s just lurking.
